about: Heidelberg Materials, until 2023 named HeidelbergCement, is a German building materials group, based in Heidelberg, and one of the world's largest producers of cement, aggregates and ready-mixed concrete, with operations in about 50 countries and annual revenue of around 20 billion euros. Atkore is a Harvey, Illinois manufacturer of electrical raceway products, such as conduit, cable, armoured cable and fittings, and of mechanical products such as strut and framing, used in construction, utilities and data centres. It sells through distributors to electrical contractors across the United States and in other markets, with revenue of over three billion dollars at its peak. It is listed on the NYSE as ATKR, having been separated from Tyco in 2011. B2B and industrial, with no consumer brand profile.

Selena is a Polish construction chemicals group based in Wroclaw, producing foams, adhesives, sealants, insulation and waterproofing products sold under brands such as Tytan Professional, Quilosa and Displine. Founded in 1992 by Jaroslaw Michniuk, it has manufacturing in Europe and Asia and sells in over 60 countries. Funding of 255 million dollars. Visible trade brand in DIY and construction. It sells through distributors, builders merchants and DIY chains, so its consumer exposure comes via retail shelves.

about: Rudin is one of New York City's best-known family-owned real estate companies, founded in 1920s, that owns and manages about 15 million square feet of office and residential buildings in Manhattan. LuxWall is a Ypsilanti, Michigan building materials manufacturer that makes vacuum-insulated glass panels (Enthermal) designed to cut building energy use. Tecnoglass is a Colombian manufacturer of architectural glass, windows and aluminium products, based in Barranquilla and listed on the NYSE (TGLS). Founded by the Daes family, it has revenue of about 800 to 900 million dollars. B2B building products brand with little consumer awareness.

SsangYong C&E is a South Korean cement and building materials company, now called Ssangyong C&E, that produces cement and related products for construction customers, with a plant network in Korea. It has been owned by private equity firm Hahn & Company since 2016. It is listed on the Korea Exchange, and is a B2B materials firm with low consumer awareness.

BLDG Management is a Denver-based real estate management company, working in building materials and real estate, which manages and operates multifamily and commercial properties. about: Canfor is a Vancouver-based Canadian forest products company, listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (CFP), producing softwood lumber, pulp, paper and wood products at mills in British Columbia, Alberta, the US South and Sweden. Customers include home builders, distributors and pulp buyers worldwide, and revenue is in the billions of Canadian dollars. It is controlled by the Canfor and Ketcham families and is a B2B commodity producer, known in the building industry.

Kesoram Industries is a Kolkata-based Indian conglomerate in the BK Birla group, historically making tyres under the Birla Tyres brand, cement and rayon. Its cement business was sold to UltraTech Cement in 2023-24, leaving the tyre arm, and it has carried large debt. It is listed on NSE and BSE. Customers are vehicle owners and fleet operators. Its Birla Tyres brand is known in India, with moderate consumer awareness.

Brimstone is an Oakland, California cleantech company producing Portland cement by an alternative chemistry that uses calcium silicate rock instead of limestone, to avoid process carbon dioxide emissions and produce carbon-negative cement. It is venture-backed and building its first commercial plant. Customers would be cement users and construction firms. It is a B2B materials startup with no consumer brand profile.

India Cements is a Chennai-based cement manufacturer, founded in 1946, selling cement under brands such as Sankar, Coromandel and Raasi to builders and dealers in southern and western India. In 2024 UltraTech Cement became its controlling shareholder. It is listed on NSE and BSE and was the former owner of the Chennai Super Kings cricket franchise, now a separate company. It is a B2B-leaning building materials brand with solid retail awareness in southern India.

Cleantech company developing an electrochemical process to produce cement without the carbon emissions of traditional kilns, aimed at cutting the large global carbon footprint of cement production. Its technology, spun out of MIT and founded in 2019, makes low-carbon cement at ambient temperatures using electricity and sells to construction firms and concrete producers. Based in Somerville, Massachusetts, it has built a pilot plant in Massachusetts and a commercial-scale factory in Holyoke, with backing from Breakthrough Energy Ventures and the US Department of Energy. Offtake agreements with companies like Microsoft have been announced. B2B, with visibility mainly in climate-tech circles.

British flooring manufacturer and distributor producing carpets, rugs, underlay, vinyl, LVT, ceramic tiles and laminate, sold to consumers, retailers and contractors across the UK, Europe and Australia. Based in Kidderminster, Worcestershire, the home of English carpet making, it operates under brands such as Cormar, Abingdon, Westex, Ulster Carpets and Cavalier. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (VCP), the group generates about 1 billion pounds in annual sales and has bought up several brands. Strong trade brand in UK flooring but not a mass consumer name.

Materials technology company producing low-carbon cement alternatives by processing waste or captured emissions into supplementary cementitious materials, notably its Rock Cement and reactive calcium silicate hydrate products that reduce the CO2 emissions of concrete. Based in San Jose, California, it works with cement and concrete producers, and has built a plant in Redding, California, with investors including Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, Cemex Ventures and Microsoft. B2B and aimed at construction materials producers, with low consumer awareness but growing visibility within the climate-tech and building materials communities.

SIBS is a company in Simpang Ampat, Penang, Malaysia, that Crunchbase describes as offering modular housing using Industrialised Building System (IBS) technology, tagged under building materials and construction. It likely supplies prefabricated building components or homes to developers and contractors, but the data given does not confirm its size, owners or projects. A B2B construction supplier with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: US maker of thin-film CIGS photovoltaic modules, which are lightweight, flexible solar panels for aerospace, defence, space and specialty uses, such as satellites and drones, as well as building integrated products. Customers are aerospace and government programmes. B2B niche technology company with minimal consumer awareness.

Saudi cement manufacturer operating a plant near Buraidah in the Qassim region, selling Portland and sulfate-resistant cement and clinker to contractors, ready-mix firms and builders across central Saudi Arabia. Revenue depends on domestic construction and infrastructure demand, including Vision 2030 projects, and on government housing programs. Listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul, ticker 3040) and paying regular dividends. Industrial commodity producer with regional brand recognition among builders but little direct consumer branding.

Chinese environmental technology company that makes equipment which recycles construction and demolition waste into bricks and aggregates, and produces eco-friendly building materials and prefabricated components. Customers are construction waste processors, local governments and builders, with sales concentrated in China and some projects abroad. Based in Beijing, with a Nasdaq listing (RETO). Small-cap industrial business-to-business firm with no consumer brand to speak of, so a sponsorship fit would be unusual.

US public safety technology company best known for the BolaWrap remote restraint device, which fires a Kevlar tether to restrain a person without pain, plus the Wrap Reality VR training system and body cameras acquired through other brands. Customers are police and security forces in the US and dozens of other countries. Based in Tempe, Arizona and Nasdaq-listed (WRAP). Visible to police buyers but not to the general public.

Nigerian cement producer, part of the BUA Group of billionaire Abdul Samad Rabiu, operating large plants in Edo and Sokoto states with capacity of around 8 million tonnes per year. It sells bagged and bulk cement to builders, distributors and infrastructure contractors across Nigeria, and is listed on the Nigerian Exchange (BUACEMENT). One of the country's biggest cement makers with broad name recognition among builders and traders.

US wholesale distributor of building products, supplying lumber, panels, engineered wood, siding, roofing, insulation and millwork to lumber yards, home centres and builders through about 50 distribution centres across the US. Revenue is several billion dollars each year and moves with housing demand and lumber prices. Based in Marietta, Georgia and listed on the NYSE (BXC). Well known among building product dealers, with no consumer-facing presence.

Saint-Gobain is a French building materials multinational that makes glass, insulation, plasterboard (Placo, Gyproc), ceramics, mortars, pipes and construction chemicals, and distributes materials through merchants like Point.P, Dahl and Cedeo. Its brands include Isover, Weber, Gyproc, Placo and Ecophon. Customers are builders, construction firms, contractors, car makers and industries, in about 75 countries, with revenue near 46 billion euros and over 160,000 staff. Founded in 1665 and listed on Euronext Paris (SGO). Strong B2B brand with some consumer awareness through DIY channels, and a long record of sports and cultural sponsorship.

Africa's largest cement producer, owned by Aliko Dangote's Dangote Industries, with installed capacity of roughly 50 million tonnes and plants in Nigeria and about ten other African countries. German real estate company holding commercial properties such as offices and logistics buildings, once listed in Frankfurt and later restructured under new ownership. Income is rent from corporate tenants. Based in Langen, Hesse. B2B landlord with no consumer profile.

Swedish residential property company owning and managing apartments in growth cities such as Stockholm and Gothenburg, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Income is rent from tenants. India's largest structural steel tubes and pipes producer, making hollow sections, galvanised pipes and building products under the Apollo, APL Apollo and Apollo Z brands. Customers are construction, infrastructure and retail channels. Based in Noida, listed on Indian exchanges. B2B-leaning, with brand awareness among builders and distributors.

Pakistani cement manufacturer operating a plant in Punjab province, selling cement in domestic markets and exports. Customers are builders and dealers. Part of the Attock group, based in Karachi, listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange. B2B commodity brand with regional awareness.

Canadian specialist in cellular concrete, supplying lightweight foam concrete for geotechnical fill, road bases and infrastructure, including products under the Cematrix brand. Customers are contractors and engineering firms. Based in Calgary. B2B construction materials supplier with no consumer brand.

Saudi Arabian cement producer in the northern Al Jouf region, selling Portland cement to construction contractors, ready-mix companies and government infrastructure projects across the northern part of the Kingdom. Revenue depends on domestic construction demand and the volume of building materials sold, and the company runs integrated cement plants with production capacity of a few million tonnes per year. Listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul). Business-to-business industrial supplier with limited public brand awareness outside the construction trade in Saudi Arabia.

Senegal's major cement producer, based at Rufisque near Dakar and a subsidiary of France's Vicat group since 2001, making cement and concrete for domestic builders and exporting to West Africa. B2B building materials. The firm operates a cement plant and grinding stations, and it is one of Senegal's largest industrial companies. Vicat is a French cement group listed in Paris.

Pakistan steel producer making reinforcement bars (rebars) and other long products for construction, with melting and rolling mills near Karachi. Revenue from sales to builders and contractors, listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (AMSL). B2B, with strong brand in the local construction trade. Amreli sells in Pakistan's construction market through dealers; the company is one of the country's larger steel manufacturers and competes with imports and local rivals.

Sinai Cement Company is an Egyptian cement producer with a plant in the Sinai Peninsula, serving the domestic Egyptian construction market. It sells grey cement to builders, ready-mix companies, contractors and infrastructure projects, and competes with several large Egyptian producers such as Suez Cement and Arabian Cement. The company has been controlled by international cement groups through its history, and it is listed on the Egyptian Exchange. Revenue depends on construction activity and energy costs, and production capacity is on the order of a few million tonnes. B2B building-materials supplier with limited brand awareness outside the construction trade.

Ferretti Group is an Italian luxury yacht builder and one of the largest makers of motor yachts in the world. Its brands include Ferretti Yachts, Riva, Pershing, Itama, Wally, CRN and Custom Line, and it builds boats in yards across Italy, with annual revenue of well over 1 billion euros. Customers are high-net-worth individuals and charter companies, and revenue comes from boat sales, services and refits. The Chinese state-owned Weichai Group bought control in 2012, and the company listed on the Hong Kong exchange and later on Euronext Milan in 2022. Strong luxury marine brands with a wealthy buyer base, a good match for F1 hospitality audiences.

Prescient is a US construction-technology company based in Charlotte, North Carolina, that designs and manufactures prefabricated, light-gauge steel building systems and offers software-driven architectural design for multifamily and commercial buildings. Its pitch is faster, cheaper and more predictable construction, achieved by combining design software with factory-built wall and floor panels delivered to the job site. Customers are developers, builders and contractors, and revenue comes from building system sales and design services. It raised a large venture round in 2021. A B2B construction-tech firm with little consumer brand awareness and no sports-marketing profile.

Founded in 1988 and controlled by the Tung family, it is listed on the Hong Kong exchange (0868) and has revenue in the tens of billions of Hong Kong dollars. B2B, with little consumer recognition although car owners may meet its brand on windscreens.

Founded in Vancouver, Canada, it built manufacturing plants for its wall panels in North America and went public through a SPAC merger. It faced financial problems and entered insolvency proceedings in 2023. B2B construction supplier with no consumer brand profile.

about: Pakistan's largest cement producer, with plants at Pezu in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Karachi, plus export operations, power generation and diversification into chemicals (Lucky Core Industries), soda ash, and motor assembly through Lucky Motor Corporation (Kia and Peugeot vehicles). Customers are builders and infrastructure developers. Listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (LUCK). Part of the Lucky Group, a well-known national business name, with sports sponsorships in Pakistan.

Morbi, Gujarat-based ceramic and vitrified tile manufacturer which also makes bathware and sanitaryware, selling through dealers and showrooms across India and exports to other markets under the Varmora brand. Its tile ranges span glazed vitrified, porcelain and wall tiles, and it exports to markets in Asia and Africa. Morbi is known as India's tile capital.

Australia's largest steel company, making coated and painted steel such as ZINCALUME and COLORBOND for roofing and cladding, plus structural steel, with major operations in Australia, North America (North Star BlueScope and Butler buildings), New Zealand and Asia. Annual revenue is around 17 billion Australian dollars with about 14,000 staff. Listed on the ASX (BSL). COLORBOND is a very familiar building brand to Australian homeowners.

Finnish maker of plumbing, indoor climate and infrastructure pipe systems, including PEX pipes, underfloor heating and cooling, and water supply products, sold through installers and merchants in Europe and North America. Revenue is around 1.3 billion euros with about 3,800 staff. Acquired in 2023 by Georg Fischer in a deal worth about 2 billion euros and delisted. Strong brand with installers, little consumer profile.

Birmingham-based law firm and professional services group with offices across the UK and a Dubai presence, advising on property, corporate, private wealth, employment and disputes, and with a consultancy arm (Gateley Legal and Gateley Capitus). Revenue is around 200 million pounds. Listed on AIM (GTLY). Customers are businesses and individuals. Well known regionally in UK business services; consumer brand awareness is low.

Hyderabad cement producer with plants in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, selling bags under the Sagar Cements brand and bulk cement to builders and infrastructure projects in southern India. Capacity is several million tonnes a year. Listed on the BSE and NSE, and run by the Reddy family. Regional building material brand, with visibility among South Indian dealers and builders.

Georgia-based supplier of self-storage building products, including roll-up doors, hallway systems, relocatable storage units and smart access technology, selling to storage developers, owners and contractors in North America, Europe, Australia and the Middle East. Listed on the NYSE (JBI) via a 2021 SPAC merger, with revenue near 1 billion dollars. Customers include Public Storage and Extra Space. B2B with no consumer awareness.

Bulgarian cement producer in Devnya, near Varna on the Black Sea, with a large cement plant plus the Devnya Cement and related concrete operations, supplying construction firms and building materials distributors across Bulgaria and neighbouring Balkan markets. It is among the largest cement producers in Bulgaria, serving customers in housing, roads and infrastructure.
